title: Раскаяние Насти и наряд полиции  (Nastya's Remorse and the Police Raid)

segments.t: With everyone gathered in the office, Nastya tearfully confesses to her father and Kostya that she staged her own kidnapping because her homeless friends desperately needed money. Just as she begs their forgiveness, a squad of police officers called by her mother raids the kitchen.
Я думал, мы доверяем друг другу.
Командир, я не понял, вы откуда взялись-то?
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'What the Chef did not know.' Holding firm naturally in this beat, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Was that I bought them myself.' Barinov cuts in honestly watching Nastya, making his position completely clear.
'They needed the money very badly.' Addressing the money in this beat, Kostya centers the remark on "dengi" ("money") without any extra fuss.

'Could you not simply have asked me for it?' Pushing back dryly with Kostya, Nastya leans on "nelzya" ("it is not allowed, one must not"), which carries the whole predicate in Russian without needing "it is".
'You could have at least warned me.' Barinov follows up pointedly around Nastya, steering the talk right where he wants it.
Я думал, мы доверяем друг другу.
'I thought we trusted each other.' Pointing to the friend at once, Kostya lands on "doveryayem" ("trust", built on "doveryat") to keep the statement grounded.
'Kostik, please forgive me.' Nastya promptly voices this personal apology for Kostya using "prosti" ("forgive me") — the close, informal way to say "forgive me" or "I'm sorry" to someone dear.
'Dad, forgive me.' Barinov promptly chooses this personal apology in front of Nastya using "prosti" ("forgive me") — the close, informal way to say "forgive me" or "I'm sorry" to someone dear.

'Forgive me, all of you.' Kostya smoothly voices this formal apology in the exchange using "prostite" ("forgive me") — a warmer, more earnest polite apology that literally asks someone to forgive you.
'The restrooms and locker rooms are clear.' Addressing the changing room with Kostya, Nastya links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'Go check the storage room.' Barinov proceeds promptly in this moment, testing Nastya's reaction in the middle of the exchange.
Командир, я не понял, вы откуда взялись-то?
'Officer, I do not understand, where did you guys come from?' Pointing to the commander at once, Kostya uses "komandir" ("commander") to carry the main weight of the thought.
'I was the one who called them.' Pushing back naturally in front of Kostya, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Я думал, мы доверяем друг другу.
Командир, я не понял, вы откуда взялись-то?

That wraps up this scene as nastya confesses to her father and Kostya that she staged the kidnapping to help her homeless friends, right before police officers summoned by her mother storm in. Until next time!
